newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan public fund still buying US notes-dealers.
newsitem.headline: Japan public fund still buying US notes-dealers.

text.p: A major Japanese public fund has continued to buy substantial amounts of short-term U.S. government securities and dollars after the Group of Seven (G7) nations meeting on Saturday, dealers said on Wednesday.
The public fund body had to convert yen into dollars on the foreign exchange market to buy the U.S. Treasuries.
"One major public fund continues to buy shorter-term securities even after the G7 meeting," said one bond dealer.
The G7 meeting indicated a desire for currency stability and said the dollar has surged enough.
The dealer said buy orders for U.S. securities come in a large lot almost every day and such moves might be aimed at switching assets from maturing U.S. securities.

Some currency dealers said there was talk that a Japanese public fund body, possibly the Postal Life Insurance Bureau (Kampo), one of the world's largest public funds, might have bought dollars on Wednesday in Tokyo.
Dealers said that the public fund buying was a driving force behind the dollar's rise against the yen. Tokyo treasury desk +81-3-3432-1396
